title: Open/Add Specific Colorways
description:
The new update to our Colorway Editor in CLO 2025.1 allows you to choose specific colorways to import when opening or adding garment files.

markdown_content: ## Introduction to Colorways and Adding Garments This section explains how to manage colorways in the Production module and how to add garments with specific colorways in CLO software. It covers basic navigation and the process of incorporating a cover-up garment alongside a bathing suit with multiple colorways. In the Production module under Colorway, you can view and manage different colorways assigned to a garment. For example, starting with a bathing suit that has four distinct colorways, you can add another garment, such as a cover-up, by going to **File > Add Garment** and selecting the cover-up. After adding the new garment, you return to **Production > Colorway**, where you have the option to choose colorways for the new garment. You can select **All** or **Custom** colorways. Choosing **Custom** lets you pick specific colorways to apply to the added garment. For instance, selecting the four existing colorways and confirming will add the cover-up in those colorways, synchronizing it with the bathing suit's color variations. ## Editing Colorway Details and Unlinking Colors This section describes how to customize colors within a specific colorway, including editing individual color elements and unlinking colors to prevent simultaneous changes. Once colorways are loaded, you can go into a particular colorway (e.g., Colorway 2) and edit individual color elements such as buttons. Using the color dropdown menu, you can select a color element and change its color directly. A key feature is the ability to **unlink** colors. If color elements are linked, changing one color will affect all linked elements, which is sometimes undesirable. By unlinking these colors, you can edit each part independently without affecting the others. This unlinking is done quickly and easily in the colorway editor, allowing precise customization of colors within a garment. ## Exporting High-Quality Colorway Images This section explains how to save higher-resolution images of colorways for better visualization and presentation purposes. You can export images of your colorways by selecting **Save Image** and then choosing **Colorway Editor**. Here, you can adjust the scale, for example, setting the image to 4x size to generate a much larger and higher-quality image. This approach helps to view all colorways clearly without needing to render each one individually. The process simplifies reviewing and sharing color variations without extra rendering time. ## Adding Additional Colorways and Synchronizing Garments This section details how to add extra colorways beyond the initial set and how CLO handles colorways across multiple garments when new colorways are introduced. You can add more colorways to a garment by creating two or more additional colorways. After increasing the total colorways (e.g., from four to six), you might want to update the garments accordingly. If you add a garment like a cover-up after creating extra colorways, and select **All Colorways** during the garment addition, CLO will apply existing colorways to the new garment. However, since the cover-up was initially assigned only four colorways, the software assigns the first colorway to the extra colorways (five and six) by default. This behavior means that the new colorways beyond the original set inherit the first colorway's colors for the newly added garment unless manually adjusted. This synchronization mechanism ensures all garments have consistent colorway assignments but may require manual edits for unique colors in the additional colorways. --- This document covers fundamental and intermediate steps for managing, editing, exporting, and expanding colorways in CLO, focusing on adding garments with specific colorways, editing colors independently, exporting large images, and handling additional colorways across garments.
